checks.title: Transaction group
checks.detail: Opened ${var.transaction}, the transaction group that stood out.

checks.title: Trace path
checks.detail: Followed one typical trace through the request.

answer.evidence: The typical APM trace connects ${truth.finding} to ${truth.scope}.

goals.title: Open the affected service
goals.concept: APM's service and environment filters decide which rates, errors, durations and samples you compare.
goals.narration: Open the service the report is about in APM.
goals.reasoning: Choosing the service keeps other services' traces out of the comparison.
goals.evidence: The service page shows this incident's transactions.

demonstration.narration: I'll open ${var.service} in APM to see the latency and failures for the service in this report.
demonstration.reasoning: The APM Services inventory lists many services. Opening ${var.service} keeps other services' traces out of the comparison.
demonstration.evidence: The highlighted table lists the transactions for ${var.service}, including ${var.transaction}. That shows where to look next. We still need to check one request's trace.

hints: Start from the service the report names.
Select ${var.service}; Show me can take you there.

drifts.note: You opened ${action.value}; the report is about a different service.

goals.title: Open the affected transaction group
goals.concept: A transaction group collects requests for the same operation, so you can compare their latency and failures.
goals.narration: Open the transaction group whose latency or failures stand out.
goals.reasoning: The group links the problem seen for the whole service to samples of single requests.
goals.evidence: The transaction detail view shows samples for the affected operation.

demonstration.narration: I'll open ${var.transaction}, the transaction group whose latency or failures stand out, to narrow the question to one operation.
demonstration.reasoning: Metrics for the whole service mix different operations. One transaction group narrows the question to requests of the same kind.
demonstration.evidence: The highlighted chart shows the latency distribution for ${var.transaction}, and the highlighted pager steps through individual request samples.

hints: Find the operation behind the report in the service's transaction table.
Sort the table by latency or failure rate and open the group that stands out.
Open ${var.transaction}; Show me can open it.

drifts.note: You opened ${action.value}; check whether that operation is the one whose latency or failures stand out.

goals.title: Open a typical trace
goals.concept: A trace shows one request from start to end, across transactions and spans.
goals.reasoning: The trace shows the timing of each step, and how a problem passes from one service to the next.

demonstration.narration: A trace sample is already open here. I'll step to the next one, so we can read a single request from start to finish.
demonstration.reasoning: Percentiles and error rates can't show where the time went, or how a failure passed between services. A trace shows each operation in order.

hints: Move from the transaction group to one request.
Choose a typical sample; Show me can do it for you.

goals.title: Inspect the key detail in the trace
goals.concept: Span, error, dependency and correlated log details explain where the problem started.
goals.narration: Follow the slow or failing path to the element where it starts, and inspect it.
goals.reasoning: The key detail separates where the problem starts from where its effects show up.
goals.evidence: The selected detail backs up the finding.

demonstration.narration: I'll inspect ${var.inspect_label} to see what happened there, and whether it explains the problem.
demonstration.reasoning: A slow or failed transaction upstream may only feel the effect, not cause it. The detail separates the operation where it starts from the places it spreads to.

hints: Follow the slow or failed path to its deepest point.
Inspect a span, an error marker, or a correlated log along that path.
Use ${var.inspect_label}; Show me can open it.

goals.title: Submit a conclusion the trace backs up
goals.concept: Separate the operation where it starts from the services where its effects show up.
goals.narration: Record the finding, scope, and trace evidence.
goals.reasoning: A conclusion from a trace should name the cause and its propagation: how it spread.
goals.evidence: The answer points to the trace's path and the key detail.
hints: State where the issue starts and how it affects the request.
Use the coach's answer form: where it starts, the path it affects, and what the trace shows.
Submit the finding, scope and conclusion; Show me shows the reference summary.
